initial_observation.first_contact_summary: He also complained of weight loss of the same duration. He had no history of fever, pain abdomen, nausea, vomiting, melena, and hematochezia. There was no similar history among his siblings and other family members. On examination, his vital parameters were stable. There was bilateral pitting edema of the lower limbs. Systemic examination was not significant. His lab investigation revealed hypoalbuminemia and lymphopenia.
presenting_symptoms: bilateral pitting edema of the lower limbs
known_prior_history: no similar history among siblings and family members

evidence_items.source_text: Axial contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) abdomen shows circumferential thickening of the jejunum (Fig. 1A) and islands of echogenic fat in the mesentery (Fig. 1B). Similarly, the axial CECT abdomen in Figure 1C shows enlarged oval-shaped lymph nodes in the mesentery and minimal pelvic ascites in Figure 1D.

On histopathologic examination (Figs. 2A and B) of duodenal tissue, there was intact columnar lining with blunting of villi. Lamina propria showed dilated lymphatic channels with proteinaceous fluid within the lumen along with a moderate degree of lymphoplasmacytic infiltration. Hence, the diagnosis of duodenal lymphangiectasia was confirmed.

The patient was started with a high-protein diet. Long-chain triglycerides were replaced with medium-chain triglycerides. He was regularly followed up in the hospital. On reassessments, there was a gradual improvement in his symptoms.
